Is it better to buy all your parts at once or one at a time?

It's always good to hold out until a sale, but if there's a sale you just can't pass up, don't pass it up. I was going to get a 780 ti when it was marked down but I didn't even have my motherboard yet so I waited and it was the worst mistake I could have made. Had to the 780 instead.

If you can, wait until November. The workup to Black Friday is remarkable for sales. If you do it this way I would say do it within a two week scale so you can test all your parts together within the 30 day window.

Well, as the tattoo on my forehead reads, I have poor impulse control. The last time I set out to incrementally update my PC(an unfortunate incident with a chocolate stout - still worked but smelled a bit odd), I ended up rebuilding the entire thing. I'm of the opinion that your time and enjoyment are worth more than months of waiting and whatever small amounts you might save now that you're getting those real paychecks. Shop with Amazon, check for deals with InvisibleHand and PCPartPicker, and have that glorious bundle dropped off at your doorstep.

Sidenote, I might bump up the power supply to clear the road for a second 980 Ti at some point. They're not that expensive, but plugging everything back in is a pain...
I'd buy all at once. Unless you are willing to wait till a black friday or other major sale is happening. Once you have your rig built you can go to piece meal upgrading as necessary.

As far as your build, do you already have a good monitor? Getting a 980 Ti for a 1080p60 and... 1280 x 1024 monitor is a waste. I have a single 980 Ti on a 1440p 144Hz monitor and get 90-130 fps (depending on the map) with Bf4 maxed out with 2x MSAA.
Honestly, I don't know much about monitors but "I need a 21 and a 17 inch monitor to fit on my desk. Monitors make pretty colors." I'm open to suggestions

Check out Techpowerup!'s review of the 980 Ti

http://www.techpowerup.com/reviews/NVIDIA/GeForce_GTX_980_Ti/31.html

With the exception of a couple games, a 970 easily able to run games maxed out at 60+ fps at 1080p. A 980 Ti is total overkill.

For starters, you should look into the budget 1440p IPS/PLS panels like the QNIX QX2710 or get a good 1080p 144Hz monitor. They're in the $250-$300 range. Or, look in to a GSync monitor. They start at $400 and having used FreeSync and GSync, I highly recommend it.

Getting a 980 Ti for a 1080p 60Hz monitor is like putting a 650 horse power engine into a car that's limited to and can never exceed 60 MPH.

Personally, I did everything one or two at a time (Money is short) and usually bought them during sale periods. There will be sales on them! Once they do go on sale I look around local stores (like best buy or Fry's) and price match them.

All at once. My own experience from back when I was broke as fuck is that mixing parts of different vintages tends to have a negative effect on system stability. About the only exception I can think of is the PSU. A good PSU is timeless.

Best regards, Sir_Charming

I'll kick it off, so my family name would be Gottfried (Joffrey with a light g sound). My family has been using it as far back as we can go which is early 1500s.

However since my family took a boat over here in the 1850s our native language has change to English and well Gottfried is a German name so since then if that version was used it would be a middle name. However the English versions of it; Joffrey, Jeffrey, and my favorite Godfrey are still used as a first or middle name almost every generation still.

Since I'm very traditional I'm planning on (hoping my future wife supports me) using Gottfried as a middle name or Godfrey as a first name on a son if I ever have one.

My family name does mean shit apart from that one of my predecessors was a peasant and belonged to a landlord who had a very regular name. So when the time came in the 19th century to free the peasants, they were usually given the name of their landlord with the postposition meaning that they belonged to that landlord.

e.g. if my predecessor's landlord's name were Ivan, they were given Ivanoff as their last name. So, hence my last name (not really Ivanoff, but in the same vein).

A pretty common occurrence in Russia.
